column1: When is binaryData required instead of data?
column2: When the content is genuinely binary and would be corrupted by UTF-8 handling — e.g. a DER-format certificate or compiled protobuf schema. PEM certs are text and belong in data.

column1: Can the same key exist in both data and binaryData on one ConfigMap?
column2: No — the API server rejects this as a duplicate key overlap between the two fields.

column1: What does immutable: true actually eliminate at the control-plane level?
column2: The kubelet watch connection for that ConfigMap on every node consuming it — at scale this measurably reduces API server goroutine count, memory, and event load.

column1: What is the ConfigMap size limit, and what's included in it?
column2: 1 MiB total, combining all data and binaryData values together — enforced by the API server at creation and update time.

column1: Do envFrom-loaded ConfigMap values ever update in a running container?
column2: No — never, regardless of how long you wait. The container runtime bakes the value into the process environment once at start; only a pod restart picks up a change.

column1: Do volume-mounted ConfigMap values update in a running container?
column2: Yes — eventually, within one kubelet syncFrequency window (effective default 1 minute), via an atomic symlink swap, with no pod restart needed.

column1: Why does kubelet use a two-level ..data symlink instead of overwriting the file directly?
column2: A direct overwrite isn't atomic — a reader could see a half-written file. The two-level chain lets kubelet write new content to a fresh directory, then atomically rename() the ..data symlink to point at it.

column1: Can envFrom rename a ConfigMap key when injecting it as an env var?
column2: No — only env.valueFrom.configMapKeyRef supports renaming; envFrom always uses the ConfigMap's key name as-is.

column1: If optional: true and the referenced ConfigMap/key is missing, is the env var set to an empty string?
column2: No — it's absent entirely, not present-with-empty-value. printenv on it returns nothing and a non-zero exit code.

column1: Does $(VAR_NAME) substitution in command/args see variables loaded via envFrom?
column2: No — it only sees variables explicitly declared in the same env[] list; envFrom-loaded variables are invisible to it.

column1: Is $(VAR_NAME) shell substitution or Kubernetes substitution?
column2: Kubernetes substitution — it happens on the raw command string before the container runtime ever sees it, which is why it also works in exec-form commands with no shell at all.

column1: What happens if a pod references a nonexistent ConfigMap without optional: true?
column2: The pod is stuck in CreateContainerConfigError, retrying indefinitely, until the ConfigMap is created — no manual pod restart is needed once it exists.

column1: Why does a subPath-mounted ConfigMap file never get live updates?
column2: subPath bind-mounts the file directly into the container, bypassing the ..data/ symlink chain entirely — the atomic rename() that updates ..data never touches a bind-mounted file.
